email.subject1: a signal play for Sonatype federal
email.body1:
Otis, saw Sonatype released its 2026 supply chain report just as OMB's M-26-05 moves agencies to risk-based SBOM requirements.

A federal moment like that usually opens more agency accounts than the team can cover before reps reach them all, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Sonatype's federal segment off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Otis, quick follow-up for Sonatype.

As the new federal mandates create demand, agency pipeline targets usually climb faster than headcount can. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your federal team needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Otis, last bit of proof for Sonatype.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your federal team's reply rate likely compares to peers. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Otis, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling federal pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters, and the new SBOM mandates keep a team busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your federal motion? I will tailor it to Sonatype either way.
